summary: Two dated sightings of British Columbia Place Ltd.’s identity, from the closed reconstruction branch codex/bc-place-historical-vector-20261103 (PR #45), whose own redraw main does not use, since main’s 1983 rebuild covers the same design: a 22 September 1982 newspaper advertisement with the same outlined symbol, kept as a version of the 1983 rebuild, and the Spring 1984 newsletter’s different symbol in a blue disc, kept as its own design. The branch’s README and evidence register are kept beside this file.

assets.label: British Columbia Place Ltd.: Symbol and wordmark, 1982 newspaper advertisement
assets.publisher: British Columbia Place Ltd.; advertisement in the Gulf Islands Driftwood
assets.sourceLocator: Gulf Islands Driftwood, 22 September 1982, printed page 6: the corporation’s advertisement “Already Paying Its Way” (lower right)
assets.dateNote: The newspaper’s date: in use by then, nine months before the stadium opened. It does not date the design’s introduction.
assets.notes: The outlined b/c/p symbol and the staggered three-line name, over the advertisement’s headline: the same design as the 1983 programme’s, a year earlier.
assets.fidelityNote: A crop of the newspaper PDF’s embedded greyscale scan at its own resolution (image xref 22, pixels 1440–2080 across and 2490–2810 down), with no resampling or cleanup. Made for the closed BC Place reconstruction branch (PR #45) and kept here as a dated sighting.

assets.label: British Columbia Place Ltd.: Symbol in a blue disc, 1984 newsletter
assets.designLabel: British Columbia Place Ltd.: Symbol in a blue disc
assets.publisher: British Columbia Place Ltd., BC Place Update; Museum of Vancouver H2025.7.1
assets.sourceLocator: Museum of Vancouver H2025.7.1, BC Place Update, Spring Issue 1984: masthead of the front page
assets.dateNote: The issue’s season and year, printed on it. The museum names Ray Dykes, BC Place’s head of public relations, as the newsletter’s author; that is not evidence of who designed the mark.
assets.notes: The b/c/p symbol solid white inside a royal-blue disc, beside “british columbia place” on three flush-left lines in black: a different arrangement from the outlined 1982–83 symbol, without its parallel outline.
assets.fidelityNote: An unmodified crop of the museum’s largest public image of the issue (pixels 130–825 across, 135–340 down), with the newsletter’s UPDATE title and issue line kept as printed. Raster; colours as the museum photographed them.
